raw_response:
I've been growing cotton on this land my whole life. Forty-five years. I know this soil — the way it sits after a hard winter, how it drains near the east edge, when to push the water in and when to hold back. At my age and with just the two of us managing things (my wife picks up work off the farm sometimes), I'm not changing what works.

Cotton is all I grow. Seven mu, same as always. The county extension pushed us toward Bt hybrid seeds back in the late 90s and I made the switch — it cut my bollworm spraying way down. I'll stick with hybrid. No reason to go back to traditional seed and deal with bollworm the hard way again.

I plough in late autumn or early spring before planting. The soil here in Quzhou is heavy enough that rotary alone doesn't break it up right. Plough is what I do.

Fertilizer — I base dress before planting and topdress at bud and boll stage. Eighteen kilos of nitrogen per mu spread across the season feels right from experience. A bit of phosphorus and potassium in the base dressing.

The well is reliable. I irrigate at seedling, bud, first flower, peak boll-set, and one more at late boll. Five times usually. If it rains right I might skip one.

For pesticide, even with Bt cotton the aphids and spider mites still come in July. I spray five or six times a season. I'll say five and add one if the mites get bad.

I expect around 280 jin per mu — seed cotton. Some years better, some worse. That's what I plan for.
